title: Exposure Before Finish
shortDefinition: Exposure means opening the finish line before applying finishing force — if the path is not clear, it is not time to squeeze.
whyItMatters: Many people squeeze early and lose position or expose their back; exposure before finish keeps you in the right hierarchy.
deepExplanation: Exposure appears in every submission: RNC needs the path under the chin, arm triangle needs shoulder-line trap, leg locks need heel exposure. Finish should come only after confirming the finish line is open.
beginnerView: Ask: can you see the finish path clearly, or are you just hoping?
advancedView: Design the whole chain so each opponent reaction opens a different exposure line.

ifThenExamples.if: If you lose Exposure Before Finish during the exchange.
ifThenExamples.then: Stop accelerating, recover the nearest body structure, then continue the technique.
ifThenExamples.why: Modern no-gi punishes forceful continuation after structure is lost.

ifThenExamples.if: If the opponent correctly answers your first line.
ifThenExamples.then: Use Exposure Before Finish to switch to a safer branch instead of forcing the same line.
ifThenExamples.why: A good concept turns the opponent’s reaction into information for the next decision.

commonMisunderstandings.misunderstanding: Exposure Before Finish is a single technical trick.
commonMisunderstandings.correction: Treat it as a decision rule that appears across many positions.

commonMisunderstandings.misunderstanding: Understanding the concept automatically makes it work live.
commonMisunderstandings.correction: The concept needs body signals, short cues, and positional rolling.

trainingCues: Name Exposure Before Finish before adding force.
Find the body signal instead of guessing generally.
If structure is lost, reset one layer first.
Drill slowly, then test with progressive resistance.
